blocks.text: It is raining heavily in Colombo.
Kasun stands beside his small three-wheeler, selling homemade short eats and tea to office workers.
His clothes are simple, but his eyes are full of ambition.
One day… I'll have my own restaurant.
blocks.speaker: Kasun

blocks.text: Across the road, Anudi steps out of a comfortable family car, dressed elegantly and holding an umbrella.
She accidentally drops her phone near Kasun's three-wheeler.
Kasun picks it up and runs after her.
Miss! Your phone!
blocks.speaker: Kasun

blocks.text: Anudi turns around.
Oh… thank you.
blocks.speaker: Anudi

blocks.text: She looks at his little business.
You made all this yourself?
blocks.speaker: Anudi

blocks.text: Kasun smiles.
Started with Rs. 5,000. I'm trying to make it bigger.
blocks.speaker: Kasun

blocks.text: Anudi smiles back.
Suddenly, her phone rings. It is her father.
Anudi, where are you? Come home. We need to talk about your marriage.
blocks.speaker: Father

blocks.text: Her smile disappears.
She looks at Kasun one more time.
Maybe… I'll see you again.
blocks.speaker: Anudi

blocks.text: She walks away.
Kasun watches her leave.
He had no idea that this meeting was about to change his life.
blocks.speaker: Narrator

place.name: A Colombo roadside in heavy rain

treatment.logline: In a monsoon-soaked Colombo street, a young vendor returns a lost phone to a kind stranger; they spark for a breath before her father’s call pulls her away, planting a promise that will change his life.

arc.feeling: The world is harsh but alive; Kasun’s quiet ambition burns against the downpour.
A graceful interruption; a choice to act.
Warmth and curiosity bloom between two very different worlds.
Control intrudes; the warmth chills; a look becomes a goodbye.

arc.beat: A fragile promise and fate’s whisper
arc.feeling: Hope survives the rain; destiny speaks over distance.

treatment.approach: Rain is the texture and the music. We contrast the big, wet city (24–35mm wides) with intimate, human faces (50–85mm, shallow). Movement follows intention: a slow push for Kasun’s dream, a handheld drift when chance kicks in, and still, held frames when the phone call freezes them. Foreground rain, umbrellas, tuk-tuk edges and the stall counter layer depth. Keep contact implied: hands near but not touching; show the phone’s light/ring as reflection and sound, not text.

treatment.geography: Stall and three-wheeler are screen left along the curb; the road runs left-to-right behind them. The family car is pulled in just right of frame, nose angled toward the stall so Anudi steps out near the stall edge (no unseen walk). Our line runs along the curb, camera mostly on the street side facing the shopfronts, keeping Kasun screen left and Anudi right through their exchange. We do not cross the line; wides re-establish positions before the final departure.
treatment.key_image: Kasun, rain-streaked, holding her phone out beneath her umbrella’s edge, the city blurred behind them.
advice: We parked the family car near the stall to avoid an extra move beat; if you want her to truly cross the road, add a [move] block before b5.
We avoid readable screen text; if you need the caller ID visible, that must be a different beat shot another way.
If time tightens, the first rain EWS (shot 1) or the POV of the stall (shot 10) are the safest lifts, but we recommend keeping both.
